source.section: TC-40 lines 4 to 22 (Instructions PDF p.9 Line 4; PDF p.10 Lines 5 to 20 and the Line 17 table; PDF p.11 Line 22); (71) U.S. Government Obligations (PDF p.19)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 50,000.00 + U.S. Treasury interest 10,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 44,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Utah starts from federal AGI). TC-40 (single): line 4 federal AGI 60,000.00. Line 5 additions: none, 0.00. Line 6 = 60,000.00 + 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 7 state tax refund 0.00. Line 8 subtractions 0.00. U.S. Treasury interest 10,000.00: the form subtracts it at code 71; the projection does not (not_modelled), so it stays in line 9 here. Line 9 Utah taxable income = 60,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 60,000.00. Line 10 = 60,000.00 x 0.045 = 2,700.00. Lines 11 to 16, by the projection: no dependents; the deduction on line 12 is held as the cap 15,750.00; initial credit = 0.06 x min(line 9 60,000.00, cap 15,750.00) = 0.06 x 15,750.00 = 945.00. Line 17 base phase-out amount 18,213.00. Line 18 = max(0, 60,000.00 - 18,213.00) = 41,787.00. Line 19 = 41,787.00 x 0.013 = 543.231. Line 20 = max(0, 945.00 - 543.231) = 401.769. Line 21 worksheet: line 1 federal AGI 60,000.00; line 2 standard deduction 15,750.00; line 3 senior deduction 0.00 (no amount in Utah's sources); line 4 15,750.00; line 5 = max(0, 60,000.00 - 15,750.00) = 44,250.00. Line 5 is above zero, so not exempt; line 21 blank. Line 22 and TC-40A Part 3: line 20 401.769 = 401.769; credits 401.77. Tax = 2,700.00 - 401.77 = 2,298.23. The form, with line 12 at federal 12e and Treasury interest subtracted, gives tax 1,718.23; expected follows the projection. Treasury interest is left in by the projection: its inputs reach the consumer as interest, and the subtraction is not_modelled. Expected lines are the formula results rounded to the cent at the end (half up); the three-decimal figures above are unrounded.
accepted_approximations: Utah has no deduction from income, so base.deductions is empty on purpose. The taxpayer tax credit stands in for it: 6% of the capped income, cap = the federal standard deduction for the status, so the credit is 945 single, 1,417.50 head of household, 1,890 joint or qualifying surviving spouse, once income reaches the cap. Below the cap the credit is smaller than the form's, but 6% of income exceeds 4.5% tax either way, so tax is 0 on both. The phase-out (line 19) comes off the credit, after the 6%, as it does after the 4.5% on the Social Security credit. The cap leaves out the federal age 65 and blindness extras, which line 12 includes because it takes federal line 12e; the Utah sources print no amount for them.
U.S. obligation interest is taxed (not_modelled): the projection cannot tell it from other interest.
